question: We had to remove a rotten tree from the garden because it was no longer stable. Can I include the cost in the tenants’ service charge statement?
reference_answer: Yes. Felling a rotten tree that is no longer stable counts as garden maintenance under § 2 Nr. 10 BetrKV, so it can be passed on if the lease covers garden maintenance costs (BGH VIII ZR 107/20).

question: The city keeps complaining that our residual waste isn’t sorted properly, so we hired a company to check the bins and re-sort them by hand. Can I pass that cost on to the tenants?
reference_answer: Yes. The cost of an external company checking the residual waste bins and re-sorting them by hand is a waste disposal cost under § 2 Nr. 8 BetrKV (BGH VIII ZR 117/21, LS 1).

question: We pay a company to check the smoke detectors in the flats every year. The building code says maintenance is the tenant’s responsibility. Can I still bill the tenants for the inspections?
reference_answer: Yes, if the lease covers it. Regular smoke detector inspections are "other operating costs" under § 2 Nr. 17 BetrKV and are covered by a lease clause on fire safety and fire alarm systems. A building code rule making the tenant responsible for maintenance doesn't change this (BGH VIII ZR 117/21).

question: A tenant wants to see the bank statements showing we actually paid the invoices, not just the invoices themselves. Do I have to show him those?
reference_answer: Yes. The tenant's right to inspect the receipts includes the payment receipts (Zahlungsbelege) showing the invoices were paid (BGH VIII ZR 118/19).

question: Our lease only says the tenant pays “die Betriebskosten”, with no list of costs attached. Is that enough to bill the tenant for service charges?
reference_answer: Yes. A lease clause saying the tenant pays "die Betriebskosten" is enough, even in a standard form lease. It covers all operating costs in § 2 Nr. 1–16 BetrKV without attaching the list; "other operating costs" (Nr. 17) must be named in the lease (BGH VIII ZR 137/15, Rn. 11).

question: The flats have heat cost allocators and hot water meters, but the central boiler has no heat meter for the hot water. Does our billing still count as consumption-based?
reference_answer: No. If the central system has no heat meter as required by § 9 Abs. 2 HeizkostenV, the billing counts as not consumption-based, so the tenant can cut his share by 15% under § 12 Abs. 1 HeizkostenV, even with allocators and water meters in the flats (BGH VIII ZR 151/20).

question: A tenant missed the deadline to object to last year’s statement. Now he says some of the costs I billed were never allowed. Can he still challenge them?
reference_answer: Generally no. Once the 12-month objection deadline has passed (§ 556 Abs. 3 S. 6 BGB), the tenant is barred even from objecting to costs that could never be passed on (BGH VIII ZR 209/15, Rn. 25), unless the tenant wasn't responsible for missing the deadline (§ 556 Abs. 3 S. 6 BGB). Exception: if the landlord's own statement showed those items as non-billable, he can't rely on the deadline under § 242 BGB (Rn. 28).

question: The lease says the flat is 70 m², but when we measured it, it was actually 75 m². Which size do I use to split the service charges?
reference_answer: Use the actual size, 75 m². Where costs are split by floor area, what counts is the flat's actual floor area as a share of the building's actual total floor area, not the area in the lease (BGH VIII ZR 220/17).

question: We signed an expensive cleaning contract before this tenant moved in. Can the tenant claim I’m breaking the rule to keep costs reasonable?
reference_answer: Not for signing the contract, because there was no lease yet at that point. A breach is only possible if you could reasonably have reduced the costs during the tenancy, e.g. by terminating the contract, and didn't (BGH VIII ZR 230/21, LS 1).

question: A tenant claims our caretaker service is overpriced. Do I have to prove the price is reasonable, or does the tenant have to prove it isn’t?
reference_answer: The tenant has to prove it. A tenant who claims the landlord breached the duty to keep costs reasonable carries the burden of stating and proving it (BGH VIII ZR 230/21, LS 2).

question: I rent out a condo, and the owners’ association hasn’t approved its annual statement yet. Can I wait for that before sending the tenant’s statement?
reference_answer: No. You still have to send the statement within the one-year deadline of § 556 Abs. 3 S. 2 BGB. The owners' association approving its annual statement is not a precondition (BGH VIII ZR 249/15, LS 1).

question: The WEG property manager sent me the figures late, so I missed the deadline for the tenant’s statement. Can I blame the manager and still claim the back payment?
reference_answer: Not automatically. The WEG manager's fault isn't attributed to you under § 278 BGB, but to keep the back payment you have to show concretely that you yourself weren't responsible for the delay and did what you could to get the statement out in time (BGH VIII ZR 249/15, LS 2 and 3).

question: Our standard lease lists a monthly administration fee separately from the rent. Is that allowed?
reference_answer: No, unless the lease makes clear the fee is part of the base rent. Otherwise a separate administration fee in a standard lease deviates from § 556 Abs. 1 BGB to the tenant's disadvantage and is void (BGH VIII ZR 254/17; the judgment cites § 556 Abs. 4 BGB, now § 556 Abs. 5).

question: We rent our smoke detectors instead of buying them. Can I pass the rental fee on to the tenants?
reference_answer: No. Rental fees for smoke detectors are treated like purchase costs, not operating costs, so they can't be passed on (BGH VIII ZR 379/20).

question: The tenants used to heat with their own individual stoves. We switched to a heating contractor who supplies the heat. Can I pass the contractor’s costs on to tenants under § 556c BGB?
reference_answer: No, not under § 556c BGB. When switching from tenant-run stoves to commercial heat supply, it doesn't apply directly because the tenant wasn't paying heating costs as operating costs before the switch (Rn. 39), and not by analogy either (BGH VIII ZR 47/25, Leitsatz, Rn. 37). Whether you can pass the costs on depends on an agreement with the tenant; in this case the BGH found at least a tacit one after the switch and sent the case back (Rn. 29).

question: We pay the caretaker a flat fee to be on call for emergencies at night and on weekends. Can I bill that to the tenants?
reference_answer: No. A flat fee paid to the caretaker for emergency on-call service is an administrative cost the landlord has to carry (BGH VIII ZR 62/19).

question: Our building has shops on the ground floor and flats above. Do I have to deduct a share for the shops before splitting the property tax among the tenants?
reference_answer: No. For property tax in a mixed-use building, you don't need to deduct a share for the commercial units first (BGH VIII ZR 79/16).

question: Before I enter the total costs in the statement, I remove the parts that can’t be passed on. Do I have to show the tenant how I calculated those totals?
reference_answer: No. It's enough to state the total for each cost type that you actually split among the tenants, even if you already removed non-billable parts. You don't have to show those calculation steps (BGH VIII ZR 93/15).

question: Half the building is empty because it’s going to be demolished, and the remaining tenants’ hot water costs have gone up a lot. Can I stop billing hot water by consumption?
reference_answer: No. Even with high vacancy, hot water still has to be billed partly by consumption. But the landlord may in individual cases have to agree to the tenant's request to lower the consumption share to the legal minimum of 50% (Rn. 24), and in individual cases the claim can be capped under § 242 BGB, taking into account that the landlord also carries vacancy costs (BGH VIII ZR 9/14).

question: Can I still pass the cost of the building’s cable TV connection on to the tenants?
reference_answer: Not the cable fees. The monthly basic fees for broadband cable connections and the related costs could only be passed on until 30 June 2024. For a distribution system connected to a broadband network, only the electricity to run it is still billable (§ 2 Nr. 15 b BetrKV).

question: The annual statement showed a large back payment. Can I raise the tenant’s monthly advance payments now?
reference_answer: Yes. After a statement, either side can adjust the advance payments to an appropriate amount by a declaration in text form (§ 560 Abs. 4 BGB).

question: How long does a tenant have to object to the service charge statement?
reference_answer: Twelve months after receiving the statement. After that, the tenant can't raise objections unless they weren't responsible for the delay (§ 556 Abs. 3 S. 5 and 6 BGB).

question: Our building emits 30 kg CO2 per m² per year. What share of the CO2 costs can I bill to the tenants?
reference_answer: 60%. A building emitting 30 kg CO2/m²/year falls in the 27 to < 32 kg band, so the tenant pays 60% and the landlord 40% of the CO2 costs (CO2KostAufG, Anlage, § 5).

question: What share of the heating costs do I have to bill by actual consumption?
reference_answer: At least 50% and at most 70% must be billed by recorded consumption. In buildings that don't meet the 1994 insulation standard, are heated by oil or gas, and have mostly insulated exposed pipes, it must be exactly 70% (§ 7 Abs. 1 HeizkostenV).

question: For years our tenant paid garden maintenance costs that weren’t in the lease, without complaining. Does that mean we have agreed he pays them?
reference_answer: No. Just billing costs the lease doesn't cover and the tenant paying them doesn't change the lease; that needs special circumstances (BGH VIII ZR 36/14, Rn. 19). One example: you announce the new costs in advance and then bill them, and the tenant pays (Rn. 20).

question: We rent our smoke detectors from a company that also inspects them every year, and it’s all on one invoice. Which part can I pass on to the tenants?
expected_location: BGH VIII ZR 379/20, Rn. 32;BGH VIII ZR 117/21, Rn. 48
reference_answer: Only the inspection part. The rental fees for the detectors can't be passed on (BGH VIII ZR 379/20), but the annual inspection can, as other operating costs under § 2 Nr. 17 BetrKV (BGH VIII ZR 117/21). You have to be able to separate the two on the invoice.

question: We had a dying tree removed from the garden, and we pay someone to clean the playground and replace the sand in the sandpit. Can I bill the tenants for both?
expected_location: BGH VIII ZR 107/20, Rn. 18;§ 2 Nr. 10 BetrKV
reference_answer: Yes, both. Removing a dying (abgängig) tree counts as garden maintenance (BGH VIII ZR 107/20), and § 2 Nr. 10 BetrKV explicitly covers maintaining playgrounds including replacing the sand.

question: Last year I accidentally billed the caretaker’s on-call fee. The tenant only noticed 14 months after getting the statement. Do I have to refund it?
expected_location: BGH VIII ZR 62/19, Rn. 20;BGH VIII ZR 209/15, Rn. 25
reference_answer: Probably not. The on-call fee was never billable (BGH VIII ZR 62/19), but after the 12-month deadline the tenant is generally barred even for costs that can't be passed on at all (BGH VIII ZR 209/15; § 556 Abs. 3 S. 5 and 6 BGB), unless your statement itself showed the item as non-billable (§ 242 BGB, 209/15 Rn. 28).

question: I rent out a condo and the owners’ association hasn’t approved the annual statement yet. Do I have to wait for it, and when I use its figures, do I need to show how I removed the non-billable parts from the building totals?
expected_location: BGH VIII ZR 249/15, Rn. 17;BGH VIII ZR 93/15, Rn. 19
reference_answer: You can't wait. The one-year deadline applies even without the owners' association approving its statement (BGH VIII ZR 249/15, LS 1). And you only need to state the total you split among the tenants for each cost type, not how you removed the non-billable parts (BGH VIII ZR 93/15).

question: Our building has a shop on the ground floor, and some flats are bigger than the lease says. How should I split the property tax?
expected_location: BGH VIII ZR 79/16, Rn. 15;BGH VIII ZR 220/17, Rn. 19
reference_answer: Split the property tax across all units without first taking out the shop's share (BGH VIII ZR 79/16). Where costs are split by floor area, use the actual sizes, not the ones in the lease (BGH VIII ZR 220/17).

question: Our lease only says the tenant pays “die Betriebskosten”. Does that cover the waste-sorting service we hired?
expected_location: BGH VIII ZR 137/15, Rn. 13;BGH VIII ZR 117/21, Rn. 32
reference_answer: Yes. "Die Betriebskosten" covers all operating costs in § 2 Nr. 1–16 BetrKV; "other operating costs" (Nr. 17) must be named in the lease (BGH VIII ZR 137/15, Rn. 11), and the waste-sorting service counts as waste disposal under § 2 Nr. 8 BetrKV (BGH VIII ZR 117/21, LS 1).

question: Half our building is empty, and the boiler has no heat meter for the hot water. How should I bill the remaining tenants for hot water?
expected_location: BGH VIII ZR 151/20, Rn. 32;BGH VIII ZR 9/14, Rn. 22
reference_answer: Without a heat meter on the central system, the billing counts as not consumption-based and the tenant can cut his share by 15% (§ 12 HeizkostenV; BGH VIII ZR 151/20). Vacancy alone doesn't let you drop consumption-based billing, but the landlord may in individual cases have to agree to the tenant's request to lower the consumption share to the legal minimum of 50% (9/14, Rn. 24), and the claim can be capped under § 242 BGB (BGH VIII ZR 9/14).

question: Do I have to get comparison quotes before hiring a cleaning company?
reference_answer: The documents don't say whether you need comparison quotes before hiring a cleaning company. The only quote requirement in the documents (§ 556 Abs. 3a BGB, three offers) concerns fibre provision fees, not other services. Otherwise they only cover the general duty to keep costs reasonable. Check with a tenancy lawyer or your landlord association.

question: How does the CO2 step model work for commercial buildings?
reference_answer: The documents don't contain the step model for commercial buildings; they only say one is planned. Check the current CO2KostAufG or ask a specialist.

question: Can tenants deduct these costs from their taxes under § 35a EStG?
reference_answer: The documents don't cover whether tenants can deduct these costs from their taxes. Check § 35a EStG or ask a tax advisor.

question: My lease makes tenants pay for small repairs up to €100 each. Is that clause valid?
reference_answer: The documents don't cover small-repair clauses. Whether yours is valid depends on its exact wording, so have a tenancy lawyer check it.

question: A tenant wants copies of all the receipts sent to him. Can I charge him for the copies?
reference_answer: The documents don't say whether you can charge for copies of receipts. They only confirm the tenant's right to inspect them, including payment receipts. Ask a tenancy lawyer.

question: Can I charge the tenant interest on a late back payment?
reference_answer: The documents don't cover interest on late back payments. Check the BGB rules on default (Verzug) or ask a lawyer.

question: What are typical service charges per m² in Munich?
reference_answer: The documents don't contain typical service charge figures for Munich. Check a current Betriebskostenspiegel, e.g. from the Deutscher Mieterbund or a local landlord association.
